Use the search box to filter across ID, title, category, priority, verdict, and maturity;
the column headers to sort; and the category list in the margin to narrow to one topic. Each
row links to the full entry: what the problem is, why it is open, what has already been tried,
and the probable solution or research direction.

**Read the verdict column first.** It records what happened when the claim was checked against
the literature and against independent external auditors, not what the source document asserted.
A verdict is a judgment about the claim, not about the problem's importance. The auditors that
voted on each entry, and how many reached it, are listed on that entry's own page.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## What the verdicts mean

| Verdict | Meaning |
|---|---|
| [Confirmed open]{.verdict .verdict-confirmed-open} | Genuinely open. Auditors agreed and no counterevidence was found. |
| [Partially addressed]{.verdict .verdict-partially-addressed} | Real, but existing work covers part of it. The entry names which part. |
| [Overstated]{.verdict .verdict-overstated} | The underlying difficulty is real, but a claim about its severity, or about no method existing, is stronger than the evidence supports. |
| [Resolved since report]{.verdict .verdict-resolved-since-report} | Closed in the literature or in code, either already or since the source was written. Kept because knowing something was recently closed is as useful as knowing it is open. |
| [Not supported]{.verdict .verdict-not-supported} | No accessible source substantiates the claim as stated. Retained, with the reasons shown. |
| [Unverifiable]{.verdict .verdict-unverifiable} | Auditors disagreed with evidence on both sides, or the evidence was insufficient to decide. The disagreement is shown on the entry. |

Full protocol: [How this was verified](methods.qmd).
